extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, journal editors, researchers interested in peer review innovation
extracted.subtask_description: High-level guidance on desirable qualities and practices for scholarly peer review, especially in the context of adopting technology and automation. Emphasizes balancing digital tools with human oversight to preserve rigor, integrity, and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure rigor, accuracy, and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is a cornerstone of academic and scientific publishing, ensuring that research meets rigorous standards of quality, accuracy, and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and editors should evaluate manuscripts for methodological rigor, correctness of results and interpretation, and whether the work addresses an important question or advances the field. Uphold high standards even as processes change or speed up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology is reshaping peer review by enhancing transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use digital tools and workflows to make review decisions, reviewer identities (where appropriate), review histories, and editorial rationales more visible to stakeholders. Transparency includes clear communication of criteria and decisions to authors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve speed and efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology is reshaping peer review by ... speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt tools that streamline administrative tasks, reviewer matching, and communication to reduce turnaround time. Balance faster timelines with sufficient time for careful evaluation; avoid sacrificing thoroughness for speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase accessibility and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology is reshaping peer review by ... accessibility. Innovations aim to make the peer review system more ... equitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design systems and policies that broaden participation (e.g., reduce geographic or resource barriers), ensure fair treatment of authors and reviewers from diverse backgrounds, and monitor for disparate impacts of new tools or procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance automation with human judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: As we innovate further, it's vital to balance automation with the human element to maintain the rigor and integrity of scholarly work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use automated tools to assist (e.g., for screening, similarity checks, or administrative triage) but retain human oversight for substantive evaluation, ethical decisions, and final judgments. Be explicit about where automation is used and maintain accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce bias in the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The traditional peer review process has often been criticized for being ... prone to biases. With the rise of technology, the peer review system is undergoing significant innovations that aim to address these challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement practices and tools (e.g., anonymization, algorithmic bias audits, diverse reviewer pools) that identify and mitigate cognitive, social, and systemic biases. Monitor outcomes to ensure bias-reduction measures are effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster efficient communication and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital tools streamline the process, fostering more efficient communication and collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt platforms that improve interactions among editors, reviewers, and authors—facilitating constructive feedback, discussion, and iterative improvement—while preserving clear record-keeping and respectful conduct.
